# Period Grid

A year's periods side by side and how far each has come, every state told apart by icon or text as well as colour.

## Usage

```html
<r-period-grid year="2026"></r-period-grid>
```

```typescript
grid.periods = [
    { month: 'Jan', state: 'closed' },
    { month: 'Feb', state: 'locked' },
    { month: 'Mar', state: 'open' },
    { month: 'Apr', state: 'coming' }
];
```

Each tile's `title` reads "{month} {year}: {state text}".

### Default States

| State | Icon | Text | Meaning |
|-------|------|------|---------|
| `closed` | `check` | closed | Reported and final |
| `locked` | `lock` | locked | No more entries, but can be reopened |
| `open` | | open | Open for entries |
| `coming` | | not started | Not reached yet |

The state texts are the `period…` texts from the [`r-components` namespace](../Formatting.md#words).

## Attributes

| Attribute | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `year` | `number` | The year shown above the grid and in each tile's title |

## Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `periods` | `Period[]` | The periods in order; setting it on a connected grid redraws it |
| `states` | `PeriodStateDefinition[]` | Replaces the set of states, their icons, texts and the key |

```typescript
interface Period { month: string; state: string }
interface PeriodStateDefinition { id: string; text: string; icon?: string }
```

A period whose state is not in the set reports an error and the grid renders empty.

## Parts

| Selector | What it is |
|----------|------------|
| `.year` | The year |
| `ol.months` | The periods, one `li.{state}` each |
| `.month` | A period's label |
| `.tile` | A period's tile, holding its state's icon when it has one |
| `ul.key` | The legend of states |

## Accessibility

Every state is named in the key and in each tile's title, so none is told by colour alone.
